verses.zh: 以色列啊，你要归向耶和华―你的　神；你是因自己的罪孽跌倒了。
verses.en: Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God,for your sin has been your downfall![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “For you have stumbled in your iniquity”; cf. NASB, NRSV “because of your iniquity.”

verses.zh: 当归向耶和华，用言语祷告他说：求你除净罪孽，悦纳善行；这样，我们就把嘴唇的祭代替牛犊献上。
verses.en: Return to the Lord and repent![NOTE:1] Say to him: “Completely[NOTE:2] forgive our iniquity;accept[NOTE:3] our penitential prayer,[NOTE:4] that we may offer the praise of our lips as sacrificial bulls.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “Take words with you and return to the Lord” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).

The word order כָּל־תִּשָּׂא עָוֹן (kol tisaʾ ʿavon) is syntactically awkward. The BHS editors suggest rearranging the word order: תִּשָּׂא כָּל־עָוֹן (“Forgive all [our] iniquity!”). However, Gesenius suggests that כָּל (“all”) does not function as the construct in the genitive phrase כָּל־עָוֹן (“all [our] iniquity”); it functions adverbially modifying the verb תִּשָּׂא (“Completely forgive!”; see GKC 415 §128.e).

The repetition of the root לָקַח (laqakh) creates a striking wordplay in 14:2. If Israel will bring (לָקַח) its confession to God, he will accept (לָקַח) repentant Israel and completely forgive its sin.

Heb “and accept [our] speech.” The word טוֹב (tov) is often confused with the common homonymic root I טוֹב (tov, “good”; BDB 373 s.v. I טוֹב). However, this is probably IV טוֹב (tov, “word, speech”; HALOT 372 s.v. IV טוֹב), a hapax legomenon that is related to the verb טבב (“to speak”; HALOT 367 s.v. טבב) and the noun טִבָּה (tibbah, “rumor”; HALOT 367 s.v. טִבָּה). The term טוֹב (“word; speech”) refers to the repentant prayer mentioned in 14:1-3. Most translations relate it to I טוֹב and treat it as (1) accusative direct object: “accept that which is good” (RSV, NJPS) and “Accept our good sacrifices” (CEV), or (2) adverbial accusative of manner: “receive [us] graciously” (KJV, NASB, NIV). Note TEV, however, which follows the suggestion made here: “accept our prayer.”

The MT reads פָרִים (farim, “bulls”), but the LXX reflects פְּרִי (peri, “fruit”), a reading followed by NASB, NIV, NRSV “that we may offer the fruit of [our] lips [as sacrifices to you].” Although the Greek expression in Heb 13:15 (καρπὸν χειλέων, karpon cheileōn, “the fruit of lips”) reflects this LXX phrase, the MT makes good sense as it stands; NT usage of the LXX should not be considered decisive in resolving OT textual problems. The noun פָּרִים (parim, “bulls”) functions as an adverbial accusative of state.

verses.zh: 我们不向亚述求救，不骑埃及的马，也不再对我们手所造的说：你是我们的　神。因为孤儿在你―耶和华那里得蒙怜悯。
verses.en: Assyria cannot save us;we will not ride warhorses.We will never again say, ‘Our gods,’to what our own hands have made.For only you will show compassion to Orphan Israel!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “For the orphan is shown compassion by you.” The present translation takes “orphan” as a figurative reference to Israel, which is specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我必医治他们背道的病，甘心爱他们；因为我的怒气向他们转消。
verses.en: “I will heal their waywardness[NOTE:1] and love them freely,[NOTE:2] for my anger will turn away[NOTE:3] from them.
notes: The noun מְשׁוּבָתָה (meshuvatah, “waywardness”; cf. KJV “backsliding”) is from the same root as שׁוּבָה (shuvah, “return!”) in 14:1 [14:2 HT]. This repetition of שׁוּב (shuv) creates a wordplay that emphasizes reciprocity: if Israel will return (שׁוּבָה, shuvah) to the Lord, he will cure her of the tendency to turn away (מְשׁוּבָתָה) from him.

The noun נְדָבָה (nedavah, “voluntariness; free-will offering”) is an adverbial accusative of manner: “freely, voluntarily” (BDB 621 s.v. נְדָבָה 1). Cf. CEV “without limit,” TEV “with all my heart,” NLT “my love will know no bounds.”

The verb שָׁב, shav, “will turn” (Qal perfect third person masculine singular from שׁוּב, shuv, “to turn”), continues the wordplay on שׁוּב in 14:1-4 [14:2-5 HT]. If Israel will “return” (שׁוּב) to the Lord, he will heal Israel’s tendency to “turn away” (מְשׁוּבָתָה, meshuvatah) and “turn” (שָׁב) from his anger.

verses.zh: 我必向以色列如甘露；他必如百合花开放，如黎巴嫩的树木扎根。
verses.en: I will be like the dew to Israel;he will blossom like a lily;he will send down his roots like a cedar of[NOTE:1] Lebanon.
notes: Heb “like Lebanon” (so KJV; also in the following verse). The phrase “a cedar of” does not appear in the Hebrew text; it is supplied in translation for clarity (cf. TEV “the trees of Lebanon,” NRSV “the forests of Lebanon”).

verses.zh: 他的枝条必延长；他的荣华如橄榄树；他的香气如黎巴嫩的香柏树。
verses.en: His young shoots will grow;his splendor will be like an olive tree;his fragrance like a cedar of Lebanon.

verses.zh: 曾住在他荫下的必归回，发旺如五谷，开花如葡萄树。他的香气如黎巴嫩的酒。
verses.en: People will reside again[NOTE:1] in his shade;they will plant and harvest grain in abundance.[NOTE:2] They will blossom like a vine,and his fame will be like the wine from Lebanon.
notes: Hosea uses the similar-sounding terms יָשֻׁבוּ יֹשְׁבֵי (yashuvu yosheve, “the dwellers will return”) to create a wordplay between the roots שׁוּב (shuv, “to return”) and יָשַׁב (yashav, “to dwell; to reside”).

Heb “they will cause the grain to live” or “they will revive the grain.” Some English versions treat this as a comparison: “they shall revive as the corn,” (KJV) and “will flourish like the grain” (NIV).

verses.zh: 以法莲必说：我与偶像还有甚么关涉呢？我―耶和华回答他，也必顾念他。我如青翠的松树；你的果子从我而得。
verses.en: O Ephraim, I do not want to have anything to do[NOTE:1] with idols anymore!I will answer him and care for him.I am like[NOTE:2] a luxuriant cypress tree;[NOTE:3] your fruitfulness comes from me!”[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew expression מַה־לִּי עוֹד (mah-lli ʿod) is a formula of repudiation/emphatic denial that God has anything in common with idols: “I want to have nothing to do with […] any more!” (cf., e.g., Judg 11:12; 2 Sam 16:10; 19:23; 1 Kgs 17:18; 2 Kgs 3:13; 2 Chr 35:21; Jer 2:18; Ps 50:16; BDB 553 s.v. מָה 1.d.[c]).
The term “like” does not appear in the Hebrew text but is supplied in the translation for clarity, as in the majority of English versions (including KJV).
Cf. KJV “a green fir tree,” NIV84, NCV “a green pine tree,” NIV11 “a flourishing juniper,” NRSV “an evergreen cypress.”
Heb “your fruit is found in me”; cf. NRSV “your faithfulness comes from me.”

verses.zh: 谁是智慧人？可以明白这些事；谁是通达人？可以知道这一切。因为，耶和华的道是正直的；义人必在其中行走，罪人却在其上跌倒。
verses.en: Who is wise? Let him discern[NOTE:1] these things!Who is discerning? Let him understand them!For the ways of the Lord are right;the godly walk in them,but in them the rebellious stumble.
notes: The shortened form of the prefix-conjugation verb וְיָבֵן (veyaven) indicates that it is a jussive rather than an imperfect. When a jussive comes from a superior to an inferior, it may connote exhortation and instruction or advice and counsel. For the functions of the jussive, see IBHS 568-70 §34.3.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 14:1-3

1Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God,

For you have stumbled because of your iniquity.

2Take words with you and return to the Lord.

Say to Him, "Take away all iniquity

And receive us graciously,

That we may present the fruit of our lips.

3"Assyria will not save us,

We will not ride on horses;

Nor will we say again, 'Our god,'

To the work of our hands;

For in You the orphan finds mercy."

14:1 "Return" This (BDB 996, KB 1427) is a Qal IMPERATIVE.
"Return" is a recurrent theme in Hosea (e.g. Hosea 3:5; 5:4; 6:1; 7:10,16; 11:5; 12:6; 14:1-2). True
repentance brings physical and spiritual benefits! Remember that repentance is related to
personal relationship (i.e. "return to the Lord your God,"
e.g. Hosea 2:13; 4:6; 8:14; 13:6; Amos 4:6,9,10,11) as much as it is to rules!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (NT)

▣ "stumbled" The OT imagery for unstable footing is used to describe the spiritual
life. Sure footing is a sign of a healthy spiritual life, while stumbling (BDB 505, KB 502,
Qal PERFECT) is a sign of sin (cf. Hosea 5:5b; Isa. 3:8; 59:10,14; Jer. 46:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

14:2 "Take words with you and return to the Lord"
This sentence (Hosea 14:1 in MT) has four Qal IMPERATIVES and one
Piel COHORTATIVE. YHWH demands that Israel respond appropriately!

- "take" ‒ BDB 542, KB 534

- "return" ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427

- "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65

- "present" ‒ BDB 1022, KB 1522 (Piel COHORTATIVE)

Notice the repetition of "take." If Israel will truly repent then YHWH will
completely accept and restore them!

This refers to the sacrificial system (i.e. MT "our lips as bulls"). To
better understand this phrase we should add "take words not lambs." This affirms the
proper restoration of Mosaic sacrifice.

The NET Bible, p. 1578, #10, has a good insight into the repeated
use of the VERB (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE.

- take your confession to YHWH, v. 2a

- He will take away all your iniquity

Oh, the power of repentance and Oh, the matchless, unchanging mercy of YHWH!

▣ "Take away all iniquity" The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724,
Qal IMPERFECT) is surrounded by IMPERATIVES. This
phrase occurs several times (7) in the OT with YHWH as its subject (cf. Exod. 34:7; Num. 14:18;
Ps. 32:5; 85:2; Isa. 33:24; Hosea 14:2; Micah 7:18) and always means "remove iniquity"
(cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 162). It is a plea from truly repentant covenant people.

▣ "iniquity" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #2.

▣

What does the Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

Number 4's connotation is is found only here, but seems to fit the context best.

The VERB (BDB 1022, KB 1532, Piel
COHORTATIVE) basically means "to complete," here to pay a vow
(e.g. 2 Sam. 15:7; Ps. 50:14; 66:13; 116:14,18; Isa. 19:21). This refers to confession,
prayer, and praise (cf. Heb. 13:15). This passage is used by modern Judaism to rationalize the
place of prayer as a substitute for sacrifice (cf. Ps. 50; 69:30-31). Mosaic Judaism ceased with the
destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in A.D. 70, by the Roman army under Titus.
Mosaic Judaism requires a temple and priests! Modern Judaism is not Mosaic; it is Talmudic and
rabbinical. I have come to believe that

- Jesus' words in Matt. 23; 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21

- Paul's words in 2 Thess. 2

- John's words in the book of Revelation

all refer to the 1st century history. Please look at my new notes (2024) on these
texts free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org.

The above translation and interpretation, so popular among Jewish sources, reflects the
Septuagint. The MT reads, "as bulls our lips" (UBS Text Project, pp. 269-270, gives the MT a "B" rating). The
Hebrew is uncertain and the context must fill in the necessary gaps! In context this would refer to

- prayer (LXX)

- worship of bull calves (MT)

Here are the options listed in UBS Text Project.

- MT ‒ "as bulls, our lips," פרים שׂפתינו

- LXX ‒ "the fruit of our lips," פרי משׂפתינו

- REB ‒ "bulls from their pens," פרים משׂפתינו

The Jewish Publication Society of America translation, 1999, p. 1165, in a footnote admits this
line of poetry is "uncertain."

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

14:3 "Assyria will not save us" In this verse there are allusions to political alliances and the things that human
leaders tend to trust:

- foreign alliances (Assyria's treaties, i.e. Hosea 5:13)

- military power (Egyptian horses, cf. Ps. 20:7; 33:17; Isa. 2:7; 30:16; 31:1)

- idols ("work of our hands," i.e. Canaanite fertility gods)

▣ "To the work of our hands" Hosea ridicules idolatry in Hos. 4:12; 14:3; Isaiah in Isa. 2:18,20; 17:7-9; 31:7;
and Jeremiah in Jer. 10:3-5,8-9,14-15. This attitude reflects Exod. 20:4-5; 34:17; Lev. 19:4; 26:1; Deut. 4:15-19,25; 5:8.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "For in You the orphan finds mercy" YHWH is again depicted as a merciful parent as in Hosea 11:1-4
(cf. Ps. 68:5; Lam. 5:3). The orphan represents the powerless and vulnerable people of society. YHWH's people should
care for these kinds of people (e.g. Exod. 22:21-24; Deut. 10:18-19; 14:29; 16:11-12; 24:17,19; 26:12-13; 27:19).

The VERB "finds mercy" (BDB 933, KB 1216, Pual IMPERFECT)
is the same as one of Hosea's children (negated) in Hosea 1:6; 2:4, but mercy is restored in Hosea 2:1,19,23 and here! This
is a covenant term like "My people" (cf. Hosea 1:9 vs. 2:1).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 14:4-7

4I will heal their apostasy,

I will love them freely,

For My anger has turned away from them.

5I will be like the dew to Israel;

He will blossom like the lily,

And he will take root like the cedars of Lebanon.

6His shoots will sprout,

And his beauty will be like the olive tree

And his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon.

7Those who live in his shadow

Will again raise grain,

And they will blossom like the vine.

His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.

14:4 "I will heal their apostasy" In verses 4-8 YHWH speaks! The VERB
(BDB 950, KB 1272) is a Qal IMPERFECT. Healing is an OT imagery for forgiveness (cf. Hosea 5:13;
6:1; 7:1; 11:3; Ps. 103:3; Isa. 57:18; Jer. 3:22).

The term "apostasy" (BDB 1000) is literally "turning back" (cf. Hosea 11:7). It is used in
Jeremiah for turning away from YHWH (cf. Jer. 2:19; 3:22; 5:6; 8:5; 14:7; Judah is called faithless in Hosea 3:6,8,11,14;
also notice 7:24). If Israel "turns back" (i.e. repents) from sin (cf. Hosea 14:1) YHWH will "heal their turning back" (i.e. apostasy)
tendencies! His anger has "turned away from them" (cf. Deut. 30:1-10). Notice the series of sound word plays on shub
(BDB 996; see note below).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (aphistēmi)

▣ "I will love them freely" This VERB (BDB 12, KB 17,
Qal IMPERFECT) is parallel to "heal" in line 1. Grace (YHWH's unchanging character, cf. Mal. 3:6),
not merit (humans ever-changing heart and motives), is the key to the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36; Eph. 2:8-9,10).

However, an initial and ongoing response is demanded, not only repentance and faith (cf. Deut. 30; Mark 1:15;
Acts 2:21), but also obedience and perseverance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "My anger has turned away from them" The term "anger" (BDB 60) is from the Hebrew root "nose" or "face."
Anger can be seen in a red face and hard breathing. Here, it is an anthropomorphism for YHWH's deep feelings.

There is a play on the word "turn back" or "return" (BDB 996) in this context:

- return, Hosea 14:1

- return to, Hosea 14:2

- turn away, Hosea 14:4

- also in Hosea 14:7

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

14:5 "the dew" Dew (literal here, not like Hosea 6:4; 13:3) is the only source of moisture in Israel
between the two rainy periods and is crucial for crops to mature. Verses 5-7 describe the agricultural signs of
YHWH's blessings (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27-28).

There is a series of JUSSIVES in Hosea 14:5-6:

- "blossom," Hosea 14:5 ‒ BDB 827, KB 965, Qal IMPERFECT
‒ JUSSIVE in meaning

- "will stake its roots," Hosea 14:5 (but in this context of positive promises, "will take root") ‒ BDB 645, KB 697,
Qal JUSSIVE

- "sprout" (lit. "go"), Hosea 14:6 ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal
IMPERFECT ‒ JUSSIVE in meaning

- "will be" ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal JUSSIVE

▣ "Lebanon" This is the nation north of Israel called Phoenicia, whose capital is Tyre. It was famous
for its large cypress trees. In this context

- trees, Hosea 14:5 (parallel to city)

- trees, Hosea 14:6 (parallel to olive trees)

- wine, Hosea 14:7 (parallel to vine)

In context, this may be a veiled reference to Ba'al (as 14:2d), who Jezebel from Tyre,
brought into Israel. The fertility of Lebanon was from YHWH, not Ba'al (cf. Hosea 14:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

14:6-7 "olive tree. . .grain. . .vine" The three main crops of Palestine are olive oil, grains, and grapes.
YHWH gave them this fertile land (e.g. Deut. 8:7-9; 11:9-12). These were from YHWH, not Ba'al! The restoration
of God's people to the land flowing with milk and honey is described as agricultural abundance (cf. Amos 9:13-15),
but in reality it is the intimacy of the personal relationship with the Covenant God that is the greatest joy of a restored and renewed people/family!

14:7 "Those who live in his shadow" The VERB (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT)
means to sit or to dwell. This is imagery for

- YHWH as a mother bird who protects her young under her wings (cf. Ps. 17:8; 36:7; 57:1; 63:7; Matt. 23:27)

- because of the agricultural context of Hosea 14:5-7 and 8, this probably refers to God as a provider of a
fruitful symbolic tree (cf. Hosea 14:8; Ezek. 17:22-24)

It is YHWH, not Ba'al, who is the source of fertility and stability (cf. Hosea 14:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 14:8-9

8O Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols?

It is I who answer and look after you.

I am like a luxuriant cypress;

From Me comes your fruit.

9Whoever is wise, let him understand these things;

Whoever is discerning, let him know them.

For the ways of the Lord are right,

And the righteous will walk in them,

But transgressors will stumble in them.

14:8 "what more have I to do with idols" This is a Hebrew idiom of rejection
(e.g. Jdgs. 11:12; 2 Sam. 16:10; 19:22; 1 Kgs. 17:18; 2 Kgs. 3:13; 2 Chr. 35:21; John 2:4).

▣ "It is I who answer" Idols cannot answer, but YHWH can. This same
VERB (BDB 772, KB 851) is used repeatedly in Hosea 2:21-22, which sets
the stage for the great promise of Hosea 2:23!

▣ "and look after you" This VERB (BDB 1003 II, KB 1449,
Qal IMPERFECT) has the connotation of "regard with watchful care,"
(root "to bend down to look at").

This same VERB is used in Hosea 13:7 with the
connotation of "lie in wait to ambush" (cf. Jer. 5:26). Context is determinative!

The God of Israel is alive and attentive, while the gods of Canaan are
lifeless idols of wood and metal who cannot see, hear, speak, move, or help!

▣ "I am like a luxuriant cypress" This is the only place in the OT that God is described as a tree.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE

▣ "From Me comes your fruit" YHWH, not Ba'al, is the source of blessing. What
a tragedy when God's people do not know this truth.

14:9 This is a wisdom proverb much like the book of Revelation, "Let him who has an ear hear." The
VERBS "understand" (BDB 106, KB 619) and "discern" (BDB 106, KB 122) are both JUSSIVES
(the second in meaning, but not form). The words of Hosea must be read more than once and enacted!

▣ "Whoever" This closing wisdom saying focuses on an individual
(not corporate) response to Hosea's teaching. The nation was unable to repent, but
individuals can respond to God's love appropriately! Choice is an individual covenantal
concept (cf. Ezek. 18; 33). We are responsible individually because we must respond to God
individually (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT).

Notice the two admonitions related to wisdom.

- let him understand these things ‒ BDB 106, KB 122, Qal
JUSSIVE

- let him know then ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

▣ "the ways. . .walk. . .stumble" Here are three terms that describe the life of faith in images of
physical walking (e.g. Prov. 23:19). This reflects OT Wisdom Literature's "the two ways": choose God, walk in Him
and live or choose sin and walk in it (cf. Deut. 30:15-20; Rom. 8:4-5). The early church was originally called "the Way"
in Acts. Biblical faith is a lifestyle. Eternal life has observable characteristics.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "right. . .righteous" The Hebrew root is a "straight edge" (i.e. measuring river reed). Today we
would say a "ruler." Therefore, all Hebrew words for "sin" refer to a deviation from this standard. The standard is God Himself!
